newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:
Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said there would be a joint news conference by Commission President Jacques Santer and Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky at 1300/1100 GMT.
Vale de Almeida also announced a news conference by Commissioner Christos Papoutsis on Balkan energy connections at 1300/1100 on Thursday.

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said the Commission had taken decisions on Credit Lyonnais state aid and support to the beef sector. He said the Commission had decided to raise beef premium advances by 60 percent to 80 percent and to reduce payment delays in order to have a majority of the premiums given in 1996.
Van der Pas underlined that the measures did not raise the amount of the premiums but were only technical budgetary measures.

Van der Pas briefed on the informal Justice and Home Affairs Council to be held on Thursday and Friday in Dublin. He said a Commission note to the ministers would announce three communications, on trafficking in women and young girls, on sexual tourism and on dangerous and illegal contents on the Internet, as well as a green paper on new audiovisual services.

Spokeswoman Sophie Petzell said another paper would outline what could be done at European level following the Stockholm conference on sexual exploitation of children. She said the communication on trafficking in women would be preceded by a non-paper resulting from the conference on that subject in Vienna in June.

Petzell said other discussions would focus on drugs, especially chemical drugs within the EU, and temporary protection of asylum seekers. She added that ministers would sign a convention on extradition on Friday.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/854: "Les etoiles d'or du jumelage 1996" Prizes awarded by the European Commission.
- Eurostat, news release No 60/96: EU GDP up by 0.22%.
- Eurostat, Statistics in focus, Economy and finance No 1996/9: Quaterly accounts-second quarter 1996.
